statBlock.name: Syndra Silvane
statBlock.description: A retired Tethyrian adventurer and merchant who hides the ravages of the death curse beneath a silver mask.

sections.Armor: AC 15 while Mage Armor is active.
sections.Damage resistances: Damage from spells. While Stoneskin is active, she also resists nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.
sections.Traits:
Magic Resistance. Syndra has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Death Curse. Her maximum drops by 1 at midnight each day. She dies if it reaches 0. Destroying the Soulmonger stops the loss and restores her usual maximum. If Syndra has died, she can be raised only after the curse ends and only if her soul was never devoured.
sections.Actions: Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit for 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
Syndra is an 18th-level wizard spellcaster using Intelligence (spell save DC 17, +9 to hit with spell attacks). She can cast Disguise Self and Invisibility at will.
Cantrips at will. Fire Bolt, Light, Mage Hand, Prestidigitation, Shocking Grasp.
1st level (4 slots). Detect Magic, Identify, Mage Armor, Magic Missile.
2nd level (3 slots). Detect Thoughts, Mirror Image, Misty Step.
3rd level (3 slots). Counterspell, Fly, Lightning Bolt.
4th level (3 slots). Banishment, Fire Shield, Stoneskin.
5th level (3 slots). Cone of Cold, Scrying, Wall of Force.
6th level (1 slot). Globe of Invulnerability.
7th level (1 slot). Teleport.
8th level (1 slot). Mind Blank.
9th level (1 slot). Time Stop.
She casts Mage Armor, Stoneskin, and Mind Blank on herself before a fight when able.
sections.Starting the adventure: Syndra gives the party a map and takes them to the Harbor Ward of Port Nyanzaru with Teleport if they agree. The adventure puts the group on target near the docks without an accuracy roll. She stays with Wakanga O'tamu. For ending the curse, each character can choose an appropriate uncommon or rare magic item with the DM's approval. If asked for an advance, she gives each character 50 gp.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, pp. 8–9. Syndra uses the Archmage from Monster Manual (2014), p. 342, with the adventure's alignment, languages, and reduced hit point maximum.

statBlock.hpRule: At the start of the adventure, 79 is her death curse-adjusted maximum. The Hit Dice come from the Archmage, whose printed average is 99 HP.

statBlock.name: Terracotta Warrior
statBlock.description: An animated clay guardian standing watch over Shagambi's tomb with a sheathed shortsword.

sections.Senses: Blindsight 60 ft. Beyond that radius it is blind.
sections.Condition immunities: Blinded, charmed, deafened, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, and poisoned.
sections.Traits:
Antimagic Susceptibility. Inside an Antimagic Field, the warrior is incapacitated. If targeted by Dispel Magic, it must pass a Constitution save against the caster's spell save DC or become unconscious for 1 minute.
False Appearance. A motionless warrior passes for a terracotta statue.
Fragile. A critical hit shatters and destroys it.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Shortsword attacks.
Shortsword. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Shagambi's tomb: Forty-eight warriors stand guard. Loud noise makes them draw their swords partway as a warning. On any further noise, they attack every creature in the tomb. Moving quietly without magic takes a DC 12 Dexterity (Stealth) check, at disadvantage when crossing pottery shards. Opening Shagambi's coffin can set off a music box that rouses them even if the room was quiet. A DC 14 Wisdom (Perception) check while carefully lifting the lid spots the wire. Cut it with thieves' tools and a successful DC 12 Dexterity check. Failure sets off the music.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 161, area 48. The adventure adapts Animated Armor from Monster Manual (2014), p. 19, and gives the warrior two Shortsword strikes and a vulnerability to critical hits.

statBlock.name: Volothamp “Volo” Geddarm
statBlock.description: An author and traveler visiting Port Nyanzaru to promote his monster guide and deliver signed copies to the merchant princes.

sections.Actions: Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit for 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
Volo is a 1st-level wizard spellcaster using Intelligence (spell save DC 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks).
Cantrips at will. Friends, Mending, Prestidigitation.
1st level (2 slots). Comprehend Languages, Detect Magic, Disguise Self.
sections.Port Nyanzaru: Look for Volo in a tavern or a merchant prince's villa. He offers credible lore mixed with unreliable tales and refuses to leave the city. The hardcover of Volo's Guide to Monsters costs 50 gp. Give readers useful in-world lore when they consult it. He willingly shares 1d4 + 1 clues from the chapter 1 Jungle Rumors table and might let the party accompany him on visits to the princes.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 235 for the stat block, pp. 24 and 236 for Port Nyanzaru and the rumor procedure.

statBlock.name: Wakanga O'tamu
statBlock.description: Port Nyanzaru's merchant prince of magic and lore. He shelters the Harpers in his villa and takes in his old friend Syndra.

sections.Languages: Any four languages, as for the printed Mage.
sections.Armor: AC 15 while Mage Armor is active.
sections.Actions: Dagger. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit for 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage.
sections.Spellcasting:
Wakanga is a 9th-level wizard spellcaster using Intelligence (spell save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks).
Cantrips at will. Fire Bolt, Light, Mage Hand, Prestidigitation.
1st level (4 slots). Detect Magic, Mage Armor, Magic Missile, Shield.
2nd level (3 slots). Misty Step, Suggestion.
3rd level (3 slots). Counterspell, Fireball, Fly.
4th level (3 slots). Greater Invisibility, Ice Storm.
5th level (1 slot). Cone of Cold.
sections.Port Nyanzaru: Wakanga deals in potions, scrolls, and lost lore. He welcomes adventurers traveling with Syndra Silvane. He may help anyone pursuing the cause of the death curse, including selling magic items for coin, gemstones, or jewelry. He is unlikely to offer credit. Common potions cost 80 gp, uncommon potions 300 gp, 1st-level spell scrolls 100 gp, and 2nd-level spell scrolls 550 gp.
sections.Waard's journal: If the party befriends him, Wakanga gives them the journal and marks the hex where Vorn, a Shield Guardian, was found. The journal depicts the control amulet. For recovering Vorn and returning that amulet, Wakanga offers a spellbook with 15 random spells. Roll a d6 for each spell's level.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 1, p. 27. The adventure assigns the Mage from Monster Manual (2014), p. 347.

statBlock.name: Wine Weird
statBlock.description: A liquid elemental that emerges from a wine cistern when the false tomb floods.

sections.Damage resistances: Fire and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Condition immunities: Exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, poisoned, prone, restrained, and unconscious.
sections.Traits:
Invisible in Wine. The weird becomes invisible while fully submerged in wine.
Water Bound. The inherited binding applies to the liquid the weird inhabits. It dies if it leaves that liquid or if the liquid is destroyed.
sections.Actions: Constrict. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one creature. Hit for 13 (3d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage. A Medium or smaller target is grappled (escape DC 13) and pulled 5 ft. toward the weird. The target is restrained until the grapple ends. While holding it, the weird tries to drown the target and cannot constrict another.
sections.False tomb encounter: The entrance seals 1 round after the coffin is opened if the illusory sunlight strikes its plaque. Dispel Magic on the light prevents the trigger. Once the entrance seals, the wine rises 1 ft. a round and everyone rolls initiative. On round 3, three wine weirds emerge from the northwest, northeast, and southeast cisterns and attack everyone in the room. On round 12, the room fills. Apply underwater combat with 5 ft. of visibility. Water breathing gives no protection against drowning in wine. The block rises and the wine drains after 10 minutes.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 141, area 20. The adventure uses the Water Weird from Monster Manual (2014), p. 299, with invisibility in wine.

statBlock.name: Yellow Musk Creeper
statBlock.description: An orchid-like vine that grows on statuary, gravestones, and other shaded surfaces. Its bright petals release an irresistible scent.

sections.Traits:
False Appearance. A motionless creeper is indistinguishable from an ordinary flowering vine.
Regeneration. At the start of its turn the creeper recovers 10 HP. Taking fire, necrotic, or radiant damage disables this recovery at the start of its next turn. It dies only if it starts a turn at 0 HP and cannot regenerate.
sections.Actions:
Touch. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit for 13 (3d8) psychic damage. A humanoid reduced to 0 HP by the damage dies and receives a bulb. Unless the bulb is destroyed, the corpse becomes a Yellow Musk Zombie 24 hours after death. Raising the humanoid, casting Remove Curse on the corpse, or using similar magic destroys the bulb if done before it animates.
Yellow Musk (3/day). All humanoids within 30 ft. make a DC 11 Wisdom save. On a failure they are charmed for 1 minute and spend their turns moving as close to the creeper as they can, doing nothing else. They can repeat the save at the end of each turn to end the effect.
sections.Hosts: The vine controls the zombie it animates. In seven days the new creeper grows to full size and emerges from the host, which collapses. If the zombie is destroyed first, the young plant withers and dies. A Small host produces a Small zombie with 27 (6d6 + 6) HP, otherwise using the Yellow Musk Zombie's statistics.
sections.Wilderness encounter: Place the creeper deep in a ruin and give it 3d6 Yellow Musk Zombies, scattered or clustered to suit the terrain. At camp, the zombies emerge from a nearby ruin and try to knock the characters unconscious and drag them to the plant.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, p. 237 for the stat block and host procedure, p. 203 for the random encounter.
